accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE Year 2 'Living things and their habitats' statements and non-statutory guidance (local habitats and micro-habitats; basic needs; dependence), the RSPB and Froglife pages on frogs (ponds for breeding, damp cover, invertebrate prey; herons as predators), the Wildlife Trusts on woodlice (lose water easily, need damp, eat rotting wood), shore crab (Carcinus maenas) needing salt water, hedgehogs using log piles and hedges, and squirrels caching acorns that sometimes germinate (Forestry England). The needs checklist marks air as not met for a fish out of water because it cannot take oxygen from air with its gills, as the adult text says.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented habitat misconceptions (Allen 2014): a habitat is just a home or bed (step 1 prediction, p1, m1, challenge home), food alone is enough so an animal could live anywhere (step 2 prediction and the checklist showing ✗ water and air for a fish in the wood, p2, m5, challenge food), any animal could live in any habitat (step 2 rejections, step 3 body matching, m2, m6, challenge suit), and one-sided dependence such as 'bees use flowers' (step 4 prediction 'Only the bee', m3, challenge one).

lab_distinct.evidence: flaghabnd is about what a habitat provides: matching pond features to the four needs, a live food/water/shelter/air checklist as each animal is tried in four habitats, body parts that suit a habitat, animal and plant helping pairs drawn with link lines, and a lawn that animals only move into once their combination of features is added. flaghome carries animals to homes for ages 4-5, flagneeds sorts needs from wants and keeps a pet alive, flagmbhab runs woodlouse choice trays; none has the needs checklist, body matching, helping pairs or the garden build. Gate similarity is at most 9%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers that a habitat must tick every need by trying a fish in the wood and seeing ✗ food, water, shelter and air before the pond ticks all four; that the frog will not move into the garden until both the pond and the log pile are there; and that each helping pair gives both sides something. The task text then states the rule just seen.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong answers that the lab disproves: a habitat gives 'Just a place to sleep' (the pond meets food, water, shelter and air), a fish could live in a wood 'Yes, food is all it needs' (the checklist shows no water and no air), and when a bee visits a flower 'Only the bee' gets help (the pair message shows the flower's pollen carried for seeds).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions; wrong answers carry five distinct messages: a habitat as only a bed, food being enough, a body part suiting the wrong habitat, one-sided help, and a general reminder of the four needs. Each names the slip (for example 'Webbed feet are for water, a damp body is for under a log').

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 2.7 and adult at 7.4 (limits 5.5 and 10.5). Kid paragraphs define shelter in plain words and use one example per idea (frog in a pond, fish in a wood, bee and flower). The adult text names the Year 2 statements, NGSS K-ESS3-1 and 2-LS4-1 and the key words. Canvas labels are short, with tiles of at least 64 px tall on phones.

no_filler.evidence: Filler gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea: what a habitat gives, a pond for a frog, being suited, depending on each other including plants. Items cover the definition (p1, m1, m7), wrong habitats (p2, m5 garden, m6), suited bodies (p4, m2), dependence (p5, m3, m4 acorns), plants (m9) and shelter counts (m8).

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px Android light and dark and desktop dark screenshots of every step at the start and after Show me. After fixing row spacing on phones, the pond cards and need boxes sit in two 2 by 2 grids with no overlap, the four habitats and the checklist fit above the animal row, body parts sit below the habitats, the three pairs and their link lines fit, and the garden shows its four arrivals and features with the add tiles below.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: the next pond thing with each need, the next animal with each habitat, the next body part with each habitat, the next animal with each plant, and Add for each garden feature. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the needs met or missing. walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13.
